evidence: extent.lisp:168-170 `(cond ((plusp got) (incf done got)) ((zerop got) (return)) (t (return)))`, then extent.lisp:700-704 `(error 'fnn-extent-fault :message (format nil "arena-extent-read: ~a holds fewer than ~a octets" ...))`. The same helper feeds fn-pgs-fill-realize's 'history-page-read: ... N of 16384 octets'.
fix: Read errno on a negative return. Retry on EINTR. Signal fnn-os-error (or a fault naming the errno) for EIO and other errors, so a short file stays distinguishable from a failed read.
reviewer: extent.lisp:168-170 treats got<0 like EOF, `(t (return))`, and discards errno, so fnn-extent-read-entry signals 'holds fewer than N octets' (extent.lisp:700-704). An EIO is therefore reported as truncation; the store is fenced either way, so the only harm is the misleading diagnosis. EINTR on a regular file is unlikely under SBCL's SA_RESTART handlers, but it is likewise not retried.
scenario: A pread interrupted by a signal (EINTR on NFS or FUSE-backed stores) or failing with EIO returns -1. The realizer stops with no retry and signals a store fault saying the file is shorter than the extent, which fences the store as a recovery event. The operator sees 'holds fewer than N octets', which looks like truncation and corruption, rather than a disk I/O error or a transient interruption.
title: fnn-extent-pread discards errno, so an EINTR or EIO is reported as a short file and fences the store with a misleading cause
